extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, hospital finance/wage-index staff, legal/regulatory counsel, and stakeholders preparing MGCRB reclassification or wage-index related submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and criteria for Medicare Geographic Classification Review Board (MGCRB) reclassification applications and related wage-index adjustments (rural/imputed/frontier floors, out-migration, caps, and transition exceptions) for IPPS/LTCH wage index rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline for FY 2028 reclassifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for FY 2028 reclassifications are due to the MGCRB by September 1, 2026. This is also the current deadline for canceling a previous wage index reclassification termination (reinstating a reclassification) under §412.273(d) for the FY 2027 cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit timely to meet the stated deadline; procedural consequence: missed deadlines may forfeit FY 2028 consideration or reinstatement options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity data: shortest route evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation at 412.230(c)(1) requires that hospitals seeking reclassification to an area must submit appropriate data relating to its proximity to the area, including evidence of the shortest route over improved roads to the area and the distance of that route as proximity data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must show the shortest route and distance; historically required mapping from front entrance to county line using nationally recognized mapping services. Failure to provide clear shortest-route evidence can be a basis for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed inclusion of ferry routes in proximity measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to §412.230(c)(1) to include ferry routes when mapping the shortest route: “To demonstrate proximity to the area, the hospital must submit evidence from a nationally recognized electronic mapping service of the shortest route from the front entrance of the hospital over improved roads or waterways traveled by ferry boats to the county line of the requested area and the distance of that route.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS would treat ferry routes as equivalent to improved roads when ferry routes are maintained by local, State, or Federal government entities. Miles traveled by ferry must be mapped using a nationally recognized electronic mapping service and included as evidence of the shortest route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of nationally recognized electronic mapping services
rubrics_metrics.description: The MGCRB requires providers to submit map evidence from nationally recognized electronic mapping services (e.g., Google Maps, Bing Maps, MapQuest) showing the shortest route over improved roads from the front entrance of the hospital to the county line of the requested area and the distance of that route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps should be generated from such services and clearly display the route and distance. Proposed addition: the same requirement applies to ferry segments mapped via these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: MGCRB reclassifications approved for a 3-year period
rubrics_metrics.description: MGCRB reclassifications are approved for a 3-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reclassification approvals are not indefinite; plan for periodic reapplication as needed and be aware of the 3-year review cycle when preparing documentation and cost reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year weighted average wage data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(10)(D)(vi)(II) of the Act requires that the MGCRB must use the average of the most recent hospital wage survey data and the data from each of the two immediately preceding surveys. The three-year weighted average data requirement is described in regulation at §412.230(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states its longstanding position that for all average hourly wage criteria under §412.230, the three-year weighted average data is required for approval by the MGCRB; proposed revision to §412.230(a)(5)(i) would explicitly require compliance with §412.230(d)(2). Applicants must submit the most recent three-year average hourly wage data for both hospitals in the applicant's area and hospitals in the area sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: General average-hourly-wage comparison criterion for reclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: To be approved for an MGCRB reclassification, hospitals must demonstrate that their average hourly wage data is, on average, greater than their geographic area, and is similar to the area to which they seek to be reclassified. Also, hospitals must demonstrate that the area to which they are reclassifying has a higher pre-reclassification wage index than the area they are geographically located (§412.230(a)(5)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should assemble comparative wage tables using required 3-year averages and demonstrate both relative position and similarity to the target area. Ambiguity about using single-year data is not acceptable per CMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: 82 percent home-area criterion (§412.230(d)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: For home area MGCRB reclassification, the hospital must demonstrate that its 3-year average hourly wage is at least 82 percent of the average hourly wage of its own geographic labor market area (the area to which it is seeking a home area MGCRB reclassification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 82 percent threshold was determined to cover more than two standard deviations of wage variance within a labor market area. Meeting this criterion is the typical sole requirement for most home area applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed waiver of §412.230(d)(1)(iv) for §412.103 hospitals reclassifying to home
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is proposing to add an exception §412.230(d)(6) to waive the application of requirements of §412.230(d)(1)(iv) for hospitals with §412.103 rural reclassification seeking MGCRB reclassification to their geographic labor market area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would allow certain §412.103 hospitals (e.g., new remote locations lacking published wage data) to obtain home-area MGCRB reclassification without satisfying the 82 percent published-data comparison, addressing inequities from lack of published data. CMS seeks comment on this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published wage-data minimum for individual reclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual hospitals are required to have at least one year of published average hourly wage data in order to receive a wage index reclassification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly established hospitals or remote locations without published wage data are ineligible for individual MGCRB reclassification but may be eligible if included in a county group reclassification under §412.232 and §412.234.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable comparisons for §412.103 hospitals (106/108% criterion context)
rubrics_metrics.description: In meeting certain criteria (e.g., §412.230(d)(1)(iii)(C)), §412.103 hospitals are permitted to compare their average hourly wage data either to the other hospitals in their geographic area or to the hospitals in the state's rural labor market area. Additionally, many §412.103 hospitals have obtained rural referral center status and §412.230(d)(3)(i) waives the average hourly wage comparison requirement for rural referral centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §412.103 status gives flexibility in how wage comparisons are made; applicants should reference applicable status when preparing comparison analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lugar status elections and notification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A Lugar hospital that elects to waive Lugar status to receive the out-migration adjustment (or elects to reinstate Lugar/urban status) must notify CMS within 45 days from the issuance/public display of the proposed rule at the Office of the Federal Register for the relevant fiscal year. Requests may be sent to wageindex@cms.hhs.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include the CCN and either “waive Lugar” or “reinstate Lugar” in the subject line. For approval, the hospital must terminate any active MGCRB reclassification. Approved elections remain in effect for the remainder of the 3-year out-migration adjustment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of accepting out-migration adjustment when county later disqualifies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hospital elects to receive the out-migration adjustment within 45 days and subsequently the county will no longer qualify for an out-migration adjustment when final wage index calculations are completed, the hospital's request to accept the out-migration adjustment will be denied and the hospital will be automatically assigned to its deemed urban status under section 1886(d)(8)(B) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals accepting an out-migration adjustment should be aware of this automatic assignment rule and that accepting Lugar reclassification may make them ineligible for county out-migration adjustment under section 1886(d)(13)(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural floor policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4410(a) of the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 provides that the area wage index applicable to any hospital located in an urban area of a State may not be less than the area wage index applicable to hospitals located in rural areas in that State (the 'rural floor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS finalized policies to include §412.103 hospitals (both with and without MGCRB reclassification, with exceptions for dual reclass hospitals implicated by hold harmless) in rural wage index calculations. Refer to prior final rules for computational details and budget neutrality adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed floor for all-urban States
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(3)(E)(iv) of the Act (as amended by ARPA sec. 9831) establishes a minimum area wage index (imputed floor) for hospitals in all-urban States using the methodology described in §412.64(h)(4)(vi) as in effect for FY 2018; applies for discharges on or after October 1, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The imputed floor is not applied in a budget-neutral manner per statutory language. CMS references §412.64(e)(1) and (4) and (h)(4) and (5) implementing regulations and prior final rules for calculation methodology and state eligibility lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: State frontier floor
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(3)(E)(iii) requires that hospitals in frontier States cannot be assigned a wage index of less than 1.00 (frontier floor). Regulations at §412.64(m) implement this provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS is not proposing changes for FY 2027; frontier floor recipients are identified in associated tables for proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-migration adjustment data and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Out-migration adjustments (based on commuting patterns) are determined in accordance with section 1886(d)(13). CMS uses commuting data the Secretary determines appropriate; for recent years, CMS used custom tabulations of the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year microdata (e.g., 2016-2020) specific to hospital-sector workers to identify qualifying counties and compute adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS has applied consistent policies, procedures, and computations since FY 2012 and finalized use of ACS custom tabulation for FY 2025 and subsequent years. Applicants/analysts should reference the CMS tables (Table 2, Table 4A) posted with the rule for county-level adjustments and durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-percent cap on wage index decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: Under policy finalized in the FY 2023 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule, all hospital wage index decreases are capped at 5 percent of the hospital's final wage index in the prior fiscal year, such that a hospital's wage index would not be less than 95 percent of its final wage index for the prior fiscal year (reflected at §412.64(h)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cap is applied using the final wage index applicable to the hospital on the last day of the prior fiscal year. Newly opened hospitals are paid the geographic area's wage index for their first year and are not eligible for the cap that year. The cap is applied budget-neutrally through a national adjustment to the standardized amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional payment exception for discontinuation of low wage index hospital policy (FY 2027 proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to extend a transitional exception to mitigate significant reductions resulting from the discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy for hospitals that benefited from the FY 2024 low wage index policy. For FY 2027, if a hospital's proposed FY 2027 wage index is decreasing by more than 14.2625 percent from the hospital's FY 2024 wage index, then the transitional payment exception equals the additional FY 2027 amount the hospital would be paid under IPPS if its FY 2027 wage index were equal to 85.7375 percent of its FY 2024 wage index. This exception would be applied after the 5-percent cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy applies only to hospitals that benefited from the FY 2024 low wage index policy. CMS provides example calculations and notes that the FY 2026 'wage index with cap' values are used for certain comparisons. The exception is budgeted/applied per the rule's Addendum.
